title: Thinner Every Time
logline: A potter throws a nested set of bowls in one sitting, each wall thinner than the last, judging by feel alone the exact point where thinner would mean broken.

object.note: Object 10 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Attention held on one thing grows finer: a potter throwing nested bowls, each wall thinner than the last, stopping just before thinner would mean broken.

thread_out.thread: Knowing by feel moves from the wheel to a whole season of water and paddy: a farmer's many unwritten calls that add up to a harvest.

requirements: A working potter skilled in graduated or fine-walled ware
A willingness to attempt several vessels in sequence for the camera
Good light for close hand-work photography

suggestions.region: Low country wet zone or North Western Province

lesson.in_simple_terms: In the texts, you go deeper by letting go rather than by adding more: each stage is mastered fully, and only then does it look rough beside something finer. Some people need more small steps than others, but no one skips a stage.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ගැඹුරට යන්නේ තවත් දේ එකතු කිරීමෙන් නොව අත්හැරීමෙනි; එක් පියවරක් හොඳින් ප්‍රගුණ කළ පසුව පමණක් ඊට වඩා සියුම් දෙයක් අසලදී එය රළු බව පෙනේ.
lesson.the_teaching: The texts say that before going deeper a meditator must master the first absorption in five ways: turning to it, entering, staying, leaving and reviewing, all at will (the five masteries). Only then, seeing a factor as coarse (oḷārika) beside a calmer state, do they drop their attachment (nikanti) to it and go further; the Pradeepika compares the stages to cloths of the same size woven from finer and finer thread. It pictures the formless stages as four men hanging from a pavilion, each held up by the one before, yet still inside the desert of repeated existence. The texts also note that quicker and slower practitioners need different numbers of preparatory steps before absorption.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The potter throws the thickest bowl first and then thinner ones from the same clay, judging by feel rather than measurement. A wall that collapses because it was pushed too thin shows the limit the material sets. At the end the finished set sits nested, each bowl resting inside the one before it.

key_terms.en: five kinds of mastery: turning to, entering, staying, leaving, reviewing
attachment to the attainment already reached

lesson.caution: Finer does not mean a better person: the texts rank the refinement of states, not human worth, and even the subtlest formless state is still inside the round of existence.
lesson.builds_on: The gem-cutter showed attention held on one thing; this film shows what the texts say comes next, that held attention growing finer by letting go of what has become coarse.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
